content.intro: M1: Introduction to Sustainable Energy System Transformation

content.text: This chapter explores the key elements of good <ai prompt="Clarify energy governance.">energy governance 💬️</ai> needed to drive a just and sustainable transition. It highlights the importance of coherent, context-specific, and adaptive policy and regulatory frameworks, supported by strong political leadership and stakeholder engagement. Tools such as Institutional and Context Analysis (ICA) and Regulatory Impact Assessment (RIA) are introduced to ensure that policies are responsive, inclusive, and grounded in local realities. The chapter also emphasizes transparency, data accessibility, and independent oversight as essential for building trust, improving accountability, and attracting investment.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Designing Effective Policy And Regulatory Frameworks
lessons.description: Effective energy policies are the backbone of a successful and just energy transition. They guide investment, shape behavior, ensure access, and balance the interests of people, government, and industry. But policies often fail, not because of bad intentions, but because they ignore political realities, lack clear goals, or are poorly designed. This module explores how to design effective and context-sensitive energy policies and regulations by focusing on tools like Institutional and Context Analysis (ICA), Regulatory Impact Assessment (RIA), and adaptive policymaking. It emphasizes the importance of aligning policies across sectors, anticipating future challenges through strategic foresight, and continuously refining regulations based on evidence, feedback, and evolving conditions.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Ensuring Transparency and Conducting Regular Oversight
lessons.description: Transparency and oversight are essential for building trust, improving accountability, and ensuring that energy policies are fair, efficient, and effective. This lesson explores how open data, accessible information, and strong monitoring systems help prevent corruption, improve decision-making, and attract investment. It introduces key tools like internal and external audits, gender audits, and strategic foresight to strengthen public trust and ensure that no one is left behind in the energy transition

lessons.title: Lesson 3: A Holistic Energy Governance Framework
lessons.description: This lesson introduces a practical governance framework that connects core governance principles (like participation, transparency, and oversight) to key elements of the energy transition, such as infrastructure, finance, and social impacts. Using Nigeria’s experience as an example, we explore how this framework helps identify gaps, align institutions, and ensure no one is left behind.
